Bundled encoder: @breezystack/lamejs 1.2.7 (LGPL-3.0).
Project: https://github.com/shijinyu/lamejs
LAME: https://lame.sourceforge.net/
The encoder is supplied as a separate, replaceable ESM file: lamejs.js.
License copies: LGPL-3.0.txt and GPL-3.0.txt.
Corresponding upstream source: lamejs-source.tar.gz, revision 1fb0ef5fa177413107e2e107d054a9b994e3f79c.
No application manuscript or recording is included in this source archive.

Upstream notice:
Can I use LAME in my commercial program?  

Yes, you can, under the restrictions of the LGPL.  The easiest
way to do this is to:

1. Link to LAME as separate jar (lame.min.js or lame.all.js)

2. Fully acknowledge that you are using LAME, and give a link
   to our web site, lame.sourceforge.net

3. If you make modifications to LAME, you *must* release these
   these modifications back to the LAME project, under the LGPL.
